chapter: Bands and bandleading in New Orleans
title: Losing his teeth and range; booking few jobs; church tape
summary: Since 1955 he stayed in the union on spot jobs; around 1965 lost back molars, changed mouthpieces and lost high notes, books about 26 jobs a year, and made one tape with church players.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, two of them in the back.

And I always had two missing hip. When I lost these two that did it. So I think I can play about 90% of how I used to play, but I can't get up there and get those high notes anymore. But maybe if I played every night in a week I could probably do it, but that'll never happen again. In fact that hasn't happened in the last twenty years or maybe thirty years. But when you play every night you do get much better on a horn. Now any recording you've heard of me, especially since I've been in the union, right now these recordings you hear some of those tunes we haven't played in six months, no rehearsal. Some of them, not all of them. But I'm not booking much work. I don't think I've ever booked over twenty-six jobs a year since I've been in the union. That's the average happening in the week. Most of us twenty-six come into winter time and summertime sometimes you go a month or two without work. Of course I have to work in the daytime. I can't get on the phone all day like some of these guys can do. You know, look up jobs and nobody ever throws me a lead. That's how I'm not that lucky. But I've always enjoyed playing and I don't guess I'll ever quit. I'm about to bring this thing to a close, Alan.
You're playing in the church sometimes. Oh, I've got plenty more. I've got a band.

I have one tape I made with some of the fellas from the church. But I still got it. It sounds pretty good. A fellow named Kurz, Alan Kurz, played the mellophone. And Orwin Kurz used to play at Club Forest with Jules Baduk. Orwin Kurz. And he and I and his son got it. It sounded like the Salvation Army band. But it was pretty good. But as far as playing in churches, kid, I don't play in churches.
